import Snippet from "../../../../components/docs/Snippet.astro";

The Node drop-in reads the device's license document from the `X-PKey-License` header, verifies it offline against your pinned keys and refuses the request when the license doesn't allow it. A route with no gate stays open. The contract is on [Verify licenses on your server](/docs/build/servers/).

Requires the License feature and the config file `pkey sdk --lang node --write` writes. The app sends `X-PKey-License` and `X-PKey-Device` with each call to your server.

## Steps

1. **Server** Install `@polaris-key/server` from Polaris Key's npm feed, and generate the config file with `pkey sdk --lang node --write`.
2. **Server** Add `polarisKey({ config })` with `app.use` on the paths you gate. It never refuses.
3. **Server** Put a gate on each route: `requireLicense`, `requireEntitlement`, `requireTier` or `requireSignIn`.

<Snippet
  src="packages/shared-manifest/test/fixtures/integration/node/server/licensing.hono.ts"
  title="app.ts"
/>

Behind a gate, `c.var.polaris.license` is typed as present. On Cloudflare Workers, pass `waitUntil` to `polarisKey()` so the trust refresh outlives the response. Hono runs on Node, Bun, Deno and workerd.

## Require a signed-in account

`requireSignIn()` refuses with `sign_in_required` (403) while no account is signed in on the device. Behind it, `c.var.polaris.user.subject` is the account's pairwise subject.

  src="packages/shared-manifest/test/fixtures/integration/node/server/identity.hono.ts"
